title: NHANES CBC and Demographics Data Guide
text: This project downloads, validates, and prepares public-use NHANES Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Demographics data for the ten continuous cycles from 1999–2000 through 2017–2018. Acquisition is driven by a reviewed source catalog, and the scientific rules are implemented in testable R functions rather than embedded in this document.

title: NHANES CBC and Demographics Data Guide
NHANES CBC and Demographics Data Guide
text:
CBC first and second examinations
The 2001–2002 L25_B file contains the primary CBC examination. L25_2_B contains repeat measurements from a second examination. CDC documents the second exam as a convenience sample without survey weights.
The legacy v1 workflow appended these files by rows, creating 557 duplicate participants in the combined CBC and CBC-demographic outputs. Version 0.2 keeps:

cbc_primary_1999_2018: primary CBC observations used for representative analyses when paired with the appropriate design and weights;
cbc_second_exam_2001_2002: supplementary repeat observations for methods that explicitly account for repeat measures and the nonprobability subsample.

The second-exam observations are never silently included in population trends.
Official documentation: https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2001/DataFiles/L25_2_B.htm

title: NHANES CBC and Demographics Data Guide
text:
Merge contract
Primary person-level CBC and Demographics are each required to be unique on SEQN + cycle. Every CBC key must exist in Demographics. The protected left join must preserve the CBC row count and key uniqueness.
These checks are deliberately component-specific. Some other NHANES files have multiple records per participant and must not be merged until their granularity has been modeled appropriately.

      A reviewable workflow
      Four deliberate steps from source to science
      Each layer has a clear responsibility, so data acquisition never hides scientific assumptions.
    

    
      
        01
        Acquire
        Retrieve declared files directly from official CDC/NCHS sources through a reviewed catalog.
      
      
        02
        Validate
        Stop when row counts, schemas, participant keys, or merge contracts differ from expectations.
      
      
        03
        Harmonize
        Apply component-specific scientific rules without burying them inside generic download code.
      
      
        04
        Document
        Record sources, retrieval times, hashes, dimensions, validation results, and release versions.
      
    
  



  
    
      Protection by design
      Scientific meaning belongs in the pipeline.
      The 2001–2002 second CBC examination is a convenience sample without survey weights. This project preserves those observations separately instead of silently appending them to the representative primary examination data.
      That safeguard prevents 557 duplicate participants from entering the combined CBC-demographic output unnoticed.
